cold_open.hook: Meta's down 3.27% today, but yesterday it jumped 10%—turns out the real business model is just renting your AI compute to everyone else.

markets.macro_note: VIX crushed 4.1%, broad rally on softer rate expectations after jobs surprise.

big_story.story_title: Meta's push into cloud computing means Wall Street has to prepare for lower margins
big_story.angle: Meta's pivot from ad-only to cloud infrastructure is forcing investors to rethink the entire margin story—this isn't a new revenue stream, it's a margin compression trade that Wall Street hasn't priced in yet.

quick_hits.angle: Morningstar's 30% AI crash warning is the same analyst shop that called the bottom in 2008—conviction matters, but so does track record.
Google loses $4.7B EU antitrust fine appeal—the company that invented regulatory arbitrage just ran out of jurisdictions.
Indian tech tycoon betting $30M personal cash on an Office alternative—either the bravest or the most delusional person in the room.
Meta's putting a paywall on Ray-Ban glasses features—the device that was supposed to be the future just became a subscription service.

odd_thing.joke_angle: AutoCamp is raising capital to sell $500-a-night glamping tents—the business model is 'what if camping, but you paid hotel prices and still had to bring your own toilet paper.'

yesterday_callback.topic: Meta, like SpaceX, looks to turn excess AI compute into cash
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Yesterday we said Meta was copying SpaceX's playbook; today Wall Street is realizing that playbook tanks your margins—the compute arbitrage only works if you don't have to report earnings.

sign_off.callback_target: Meta's margin compression—the thing that made it jump 10% yesterday is the same thing that's going to make it crater 3% today.
